figures.caption: System architecture: from the browser down to the data layer.
figures.alt: Layered diagram of the whole system. Users reach the Next.js frontend, which calls the FastAPI server and its 12 routers over HTTPS and WebSocket; the server uses the EO orchestration layer, 73 agent modules, LLM providers, Postgres, Redis and Upstash Vector, with an optional local daemon and external MCP servers.

figures.caption: The states one agent task moves through inside a single request.
figures.alt: State diagram of a task run: Queued, SGA Relay, Tier Routed, Running and Delivered in a row, with side exits to Awaiting Confirm, which ends as Denied or Expired after 15 minutes, and to Failed, which the fixer pool can retry.

figures.caption: The workspace stage lifecycle and its multi-member promotion gate.
figures.alt: State diagram of a workspace stage: Research, Plan, Build, Test and Growth in order, a Promotion Vote gate that needs a majority in multi-member workspaces, a path back to Build when regressions are found, and an Archived end state the owner can choose.

figures.caption: The task execution pipeline, from POST /api/task to a delivered reply.
figures.alt: Five-lane flow from the frontend through the SGA relay and classification, EO routing and the gatekeeper to agents and delivery. The relay classifies tier 0 to 3, the router builds the execution graph, the executor resolves a role, results are persisted and pushed back; the tier 3 no-hires branch is a dead end.

figures.caption: The propose, confirm or deny gate every mutating local or MCP action passes through.
figures.alt: Flow of one approval: a mutating call is proposed and stored as a pending action with a 15-minute expiry, the user confirms or denies, and only a confirmed action executes on the daemon or MCP server and pushes a result event; denied or expired actions never execute.

figures.caption: The backend API surface: server.py and its 12 routers, 162 endpoints in all.
figures.alt: Map of the backend routes: a thin server.py hub with CORS, lifespan and exception handling, connected to 12 router files such as workspace_data with 28 routes, notebooks with 23 and tasks with 21, plus the WebSocket to the local daemon.
